title: Stream segment expiration and flow-control tokens with legacy SDK compatibility shim
creator: Aisha Rao
description: Problem: When clients disconnect mid-generation (network blips, app backgrounding, or legacy SDKs that close early) we accumulate small, stale stream segments and tool-call state (function call scopes, structured-output partials). This increases KV cache pressure and confuses downstream billing/observability. Goal: introduce a segment-expiry + flow-control-token scheme that lets the runtime reclaim small in-flight segments quickly, provides a graceful "soft-resume" window for modern SDKs, and offers a compatibility shim for older SDKs that lack flow-control acknowledgements.
acceptance_criteria: Flow-control token (opaque id) is issued on stream start and refreshed on client ACKs; tokens are persisted at segment granularity
Segments without a token refresh after configured ttl are marked 'stale' and are eligible for non-disruptive reclamation
Tool/function call contexts attached to stale segments are either committed (if call already completed) or aborted with a structured error tracer visible in console
Legacy-compat shim accepts disconnect signals from older SDKs and attaches a short grace window (configurable) before marking segments stale
End-to-end integration tests validate resume behavior for modern SDKs and deterministic cleanup for legacy shim within CI
No increase >1% in median P50 latency on the runtime under representative load after enabling defaults
Dashboard shows stale-segment rate, reclaimed bytes, and impact on KV cache occupancy
Rollout toggled behind runtime-1.22 feature flag and can be rolled back within a deployment window
tasks: Design flow-control token lifecycle and persistence format (segment-level TTL, refresh windows)
Implement token issuance/refresh in stream handshake path
Add segment status state machine: active -> quiescing -> stale -> reclaimed
Wire tool-call contexts to segment state so incomplete calls are aborted with structured outputs
Build legacy SDK compatibility shim (server-side) that infers client disconnect vs. hard abort and applies grace window
Create migration script to backfill segment metadata for existing long-lived streams
Unit + integration tests for token refresh, expiry, reclaim, and tool-call abortion
comments: 2026-03-08 - Aisha Rao: Initial write-up after oncall incident INC-2026-03-07 where a mobile client spike created 40MB/day of small reclamations; proposed token-based approach to avoid full session tombstones.

2026-03-09 - Diego Morales: Spike finished. Implemented token header and local in-memory ttl check. Observed KV cache footprint drop in dev cluster by ~18% in synthetic load. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8921

2026-03-10 - Samantha Chen (PM): Requested explicit handling for function/tool calls so we don't leak partially-executed tool outputs. Added acceptance criteria to abort incomplete calls with structured error and link to eval harness.

2026-03-11 - Diego Morales: Design doc posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Stream+Token+Design. Added compatibility shim scope: server-side inference of legacy close via missing final ACK vs. explicit abort event.

2026-03-12 - Eng review: Andrej Novak and Priya Singh reviewed trade-offs. Decision: use segment-granular TTL default=30s, grace window for legacy shim=10s. Trade-off noted: shorter ttl reduces leak but increases chance of reclaiming resumable state for flaky networks; mitigated by allowing per-customer override for Dedicated/Private.
2026-03-12 - Diego Morales: Linked QA plan and CI job names: runtime-streaming-e2e (job id 412-stream-e2e). Created feature flag runtime.enable_segment_tokens
2026-03-12 - Aisha Rao: Added dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/stale-segments (panel ids 21,22).
metrics: SLO target: stale-segment reclamation errors < 0.1% of streams/hour
KV cache occupancy reduction target: >= 10% for streams with high disconnect churn
Reclaimed bytes/day metric tracked in streaming.reclaim.bytes
Rate of aborted tool-calls due to reclamation tracked in streaming.toolcall.abort.rate
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime-1.22 flag: runtime.enable_segment_tokens (default off for existing customers)
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted traffic for 72 hours; monitor stale-rate and toolcall abort rate
Expand to 25% if no regressions; invite two Dedicated customers to test with per-customer override
Enable default for all hosted after 2 successful cycles and sign-off from reliability
Offer Dedicated/private config knobs (ttl, grace_window) and doc in release notes
testing_plan: Unit tests for token issuance/refresh, TTL transitions, and reclaim path
Integration tests simulating mobile reconnect patterns, SDK v1.x (legacy) disconnects, and modern SDK ACK-based resumes
Chaos test: random network partitions to validate non-destructive reclaim and no deadlocks
Tool-call harness: ensure structured error payloads for aborted calls are surfaced to console and SDKs
Load test: 100k concurrent streams with 10% disconnect churn to validate KV cache behavior and latency
